findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the instruction/criterion added to the Pass-1 discovery unit that directs it to compare the plan against the injected candidate tickets and emit an advisory overlap finding naming each, so AC1 is reachable.
evidence: 'Candidates ride a chunk already being sent, so overlap judging adds no LLM call'
'An overlap finding names the candidate ticket plus why it overlaps'

The G5 precedent at pass1.py:219-222 injects decomposition context, but a finding is emitted only when a rubric criterion/instruction drives the unit — the plan describes adding candidate CONTEXT but no instruction telling the unit to compare the plan against those candidates and name overlaps.
AC1 requires a finding naming the ticket, but no described step establishes how the unit is told to produce it.
findings.finding: The plan injects candidate tickets into the Pass-1 extra_context seam but never specifies the instruction/criterion that makes the Pass-1 unit actually JUDGE overlap and emit an advisory finding naming the candidate. Injecting candidate text as extra_context alone does not cause the LLM unit to produce an overlap finding; some prompt/criterion addition is the undescribed mechanism that AC1 depends on.
findings.location: Approach — 'the existing Pass-1 unit does the judging' / 'Ride the existing Pass-1 extra-context seam'; AC1
scenarios: With overlap=True, candidates are injected but the unit has no instruction to compare them, so no finding is emitted and AC1 fails.
AC1's seeded-store test passes only if the judging instruction exists; the plan leaves that step undescribed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Approach sentence describing the overlap judging instruction appended alongside the injected candidates (e.g. a Pass-1 rubric clause 'flag any injected candidate whose described work this plan restates, naming its ticket id'), paralleling how G5 decomposition context drives its findings.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Identify the coverage-assembly site on the NORMAL (LLM-ran) plan-review verdict path and show how coverage["overlap"]["status"] is merged there, since the cited coverage_extra seam (claimability.py:132/:153) only applies to indeterminate_verdict early returns (llm_ran=False) that return before any LLM pass.
evidence: claimability.py:140 docstring: 'coverage_extra is merged into coverage (e.g. a diagnostic record)' — but inside indeterminate_verdict which sets verdict='INDETERMINATE', 'llm_ran': False (claimability.py:141-153)
All three repo call sites of coverage_extra (claimability.py:120, retry.py:168, __init__.py:392) invoke indeterminate_verdict — the early INDETERMINATE returns, not the normal pass/advisory verdict
claimability.py module docstring: the not_claimable path returns 'BEFORE assembling context or reaching any LLM pass' — so coverage_extra is scoped to pre-LLM early returns
Overlap ACs require verdict to EQUAL the overlap=False run (pass-through, LLM ran) while still setting coverage["overlap"]["status"]; that combination is not served by indeterminate_verdict
findings.finding: The 'Recording channel: the existing coverage merge' section asserts coverage["overlap"]["status"] is recorded via the coverage_extra seam that claimability.py:132 accepts and :153 merges into coverage. But the verified coverage_extra seam lives ONLY inside indeterminate_verdict (claimability.py:127-153), which builds INDETERMINATE EARLY-RETURN verdicts (coverage.llm_ran=False) used by the not-claimable fast-fail, retry-refusal, and plan-relation-snapshot-error paths — all of which return BEFORE any LLM pass. The overlap degradation ACs require coverage["overlap"]["status"] on a NORMAL LLM review whose verdict equals the overlap=False run (a PASS/advisory outcome), which never flows through indeterminate_verdict. The named seam therefore cannot populate coverage on the review path the ACs target.
findings.location: Approach / 'Recording channel: the existing coverage merge'; ACs for index-absent/catch-up-failed/provider-error coverage["overlap"]["status"]
scenarios: overlap=True review of a claimable ticket where the index is absent / catch-up fails / provider errors: the review runs the LLM, returns a normal verdict, and there is no identified seam that writes coverage["overlap"]["status"]

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the actual recording channel for coverage['overlap']['status'] on the LLM-ran path (the coverage dict seeded at production_batch_runner.py:134 and filled by run_pass1), rather than claimability.py:132's coverage_extra which is reachable only on non-LLM early-return INDETERMINATE verdicts.
evidence: Plan: 'recorded under coverage["overlap"] via the coverage_extra seam, which src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py:132 accepts then :153 merges into coverage'
claimability.py:127-153 indeterminate_verdict docstring: 'Shape-valid INDETERMINATE plan_review_verdict for the non-LLM early returns (not-claimable fast-fail, plan-relation-snapshot error)'
production_batch_runner.py:130-134: 'coverage IS the journaled OPAQUE plan ... filled in by run_pass1' — this is the coverage dict for reviews that run

ACs ('When the index is absent, the verdict equals that of the same review with overlap=False' AND coverage['overlap']['status'] is index-absent) require a review that ran run_pass1, which never reaches indeterminate_verdict
findings.finding: The named recording channel for overlap diagnostics — coverage_extra at claimability.py:132 — is not on the code path that produces overlap findings. coverage_extra is a parameter of indeterminate_verdict, invoked only on non-LLM early-return INDETERMINATE verdicts (not-claimable fast-fail, plan-relation-snapshot error, retry refusal) that return BEFORE run_pass1 ever executes. Overlap retrieval runs inside run_pass1 (pass1.py:232) on the normal LLM-ran path, whose coverage dict is seeded separately at production_batch_runner.py:134 ("filled in by run_pass1"). The ACs assert coverage['overlap']['status'] for reviews whose verdict equals the overlap=False run — i.e. reviews that ran run_pass1 and never touched indeterminate_verdict/coverage_extra.
findings.location: Approach → 'Recording channel: the existing coverage merge'; AC lines for coverage['overlap']['status']
scenarios: A review runs with overlap=True, the index is absent/catch-up fails/provider errors; the status must be written to the normal-path coverage dict, not the early-return seam
findings.suggested_fix: Record the overlap status into the `coverage` dict threaded through run_pass1 (seeded at production_batch_runner.py:134), e.g. `coverage["overlap"] = {"status": ..., "detail": ...}` from overlap.py; keep claimability's coverage_extra for its existing early-return uses.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the intermediate consumer run_pass1 call site (production_batch_runner.py:152) and the review_plan→runner request plumbing that must carry the overlap flag, rather than implying review_plan calls run_pass1 directly.
evidence: Plan: 'one keyword-only parameter overlap: bool = False on review_plan (__init__.py:199), threaded to run_pass1 (pass1.py:232) then _chunk_extra_context'
search: the sole run_pass1 call site is production_batch_runner.py:152 (`findings = run_pass1(ctx, cfg, runner, single, agent, coverage, req.usd_budget, self._tf_provider)`)
review_plan does not call run_pass1 directly; the parameter must traverse the batch req / runner plumbing between __init__.py:199 and production_batch_runner.py:152
findings.finding: The plan threads the overlap switch 'to run_pass1 (pass1.py:232) then _chunk_extra_context', but run_pass1's only caller is production_batch_runner.py:152, not review_plan directly. Adding overlap: bool to run_pass1 requires updating that intermediate call site and the batch request plumbing that carries review_plan's keyword to the runner; neither consumer is enumerated.
findings.location: Approach → 'On demand, not on every review'
scenarios: Implementer adds overlap= to run_pass1 but forgets the production_batch_runner call site and the review_plan→runner request plumbing, so overlap=True never reaches run_pass1

findings.checklist_item: Specify the actual recording path for coverage['overlap']['status'] on the normal (PASS/BLOCK) review — e.g. carry the diagnostics dict out of overlap.py/run_pass1 and stamp it onto verdict['coverage']['overlap'] alongside the existing setdefault('coverage',{}) mutations in _run_plan_review — rather than the coverage_extra/indeterminate_verdict seam, which fires only on the non-LLM early-return paths.
evidence: Plan: 'The status is recorded under coverage["overlap"] via the coverage_extra seam, which src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py:132 accepts then :153 merges into coverage'

claimability.py:127-153 — coverage_extra is a param of indeterminate_verdict; its only callers are not_claimable (:120), retry.py:168, and __init__.py:392 (plan_relation_snapshot_error) — all pre-LLM early returns
The normal review builds/mutates coverage via produce_plan_review_verdict (__init__.py:473) and verdict.setdefault('coverage',{})[...] (:493,:495,:555), not via indeterminate_verdict
Injection lands in run_pass1/_chunk_extra_context (pass1.py:326); the plan does not describe how a status computed there reaches the verdict's coverage['overlap']
findings.finding: The plan's recording channel for coverage['overlap']['status'] is grounded in the wrong seam: coverage_extra→indeterminate_verdict (claimability.py:127-153) fires ONLY on the non-LLM early-return INDETERMINATE paths, but overlap retrieval runs on the normal overlap=True PASS/BLOCK review, which assembles coverage through gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict and setdefault mutations — never through indeterminate_verdict. The status computed in overlap.py/Pass-1 therefore has no described data path to coverage['overlap'] on the full-review verdict.
findings.location: Approach → 'Recording channel: the existing coverage merge'
scenarios: overlap=True review producing a PASS/BLOCK verdict where coverage['overlap']['status'] must be 'ok'
index-absent / catch-up-failed / provider-error on a non-early-return review
findings.suggested_fix: Thread the diagnostics dict up from overlap retrieval (overlap.py → run_pass1 → the orchestrator) and merge it onto the produced verdict via verdict.setdefault('coverage', {})['overlap'] = diagnostics, mirroring the remediation/drift/retry coverage stamps in _run_plan_review; drop the claim that claimability.py:132/:153 is the mechanism.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact code condition that yields status `provider-error` given that the embedding tier returns None (not raises) on provider failure; either add a distinguishing signal to the embedding tier or redefine the enum value to match a branch that actually fires on a provider error.
evidence: Plan: status closed set is 'ok, index-absent, catch-up-failed, provider-error' mapped to find_similar branches '[] (:63-64)', 'catch-up failure (:67-72)', 'any other exception (:83-85)'
embedding.py:7-8: 'In every other circumstance it DEGRADES: rank returns None and the caller serves the lexical results'
embedding.py:40-43 / :7: unconfigured, backend absent, 'provider failing', coverage incomplete all return None, NOT raise

similar/__init__.py:79-82: ranked = embedding_rank(...); if ranked is not None: return ranked; return search(...) — a None from the embedding tier falls through to lexical, which the plan would record as `ok`
similar/__init__.py:83-85 catches ANY exception, including a lexical `search` failure, so the branch is not specific to a provider
findings.finding: The closed-set `status` value `provider-error` is mapped to a trigger condition the cited code does not produce: embedding.py degrades (returns None) rather than raising on provider unavailability, so a provider error yields lexical results recorded as `ok`, and the generic catch-all :83-85 the plan maps to `provider-error` also fires for lexical-tier failures unrelated to any provider.
findings.location: Approach -> 'Diagnostic contract' and 'The one gap: failure distinguishability'; Acceptance Criteria 'When the embedding provider errors, coverage["overlap"]["status"] is provider-error'
scenarios: Operator configures an embedding model, the provider errors at query time: tier returns None, lexical served, status recorded `ok` not `provider-error`
Lexical `search` raises for an unrelated reason: catch-all :83-85 fires and would be labeled `provider-error`
findings.suggested_fix: Have the embedding tier surface a distinguishable provider-error signal to find_similar (e.g. a sentinel/diagnostics field separate from the lexical-degrade None path), and map `provider-error` to that signal rather than to the generic catch-all at :83-85.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the criterion id the overlap candidates attach to, the injected instruction/decision rule that tells the Pass-1 finder how to judge overlap and where to name the candidate ticket id, and how that finding is tagged so the seeded-store AC can assert it.
evidence: Plan: 'Appending candidates there' (_chunk_extra_context, pass1.py:215) ... 'the existing Pass-1 unit does the judging'

det_lint.py:46-69: the analogous G5 injected block is INSTRUCTION-rich ('do NOT count children yourself', 'Judge only the QUALITY ...') and is gated to the G5 chunk (pass1.py:219), i.e. it rides an existing criterion with its own rubric
pass1.py:221-222: the no-file-impact block is likewise tethered to the `no-file-impact` criterion id
criteria_routing.json has no `overlap` criterion (only 'scope overlap' as one of 7 cross-child modes at :878) — the injected candidates attach to no rubric that instructs an overlap judgment
passes.py:46-69 P1Finding has no field for a candidate ticket id; 'naming that ticket id' is unspecified as to where (finding/evidence free text) and under which criterion id
findings.finding: The plan relies on the existing Pass-1 finder unit to JUDGE overlap and emit a finding naming the candidate ticket, but specifies no criterion/rubric, no injected decision-rule instruction, and no schema field tethering the candidate list to an overlap judgment — so the injected candidates are inert context the model has no directive to act on.
findings.location: Approach -> 'Ride the existing Pass-1 extra-context seam' and 'Zero marginal LLM cost: the existing Pass-1 unit does the judging'; Acceptance Criteria 'reviewing a ticket whose plan restates ... emits an advisory overlap finding naming that ticket'
scenarios: With overlap=True the candidate list is injected but no chunk has a criterion rubric telling the model to compare the plan against candidates and emit an overlap finding — the seeded-store AC's advisory finding may never be produced
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the G5 pattern: define an overlap criterion (or designate a host criterion) whose chunk receives the candidate block, and have overlap.py render an instruction-rich block (like decomposition_state_block) that lists candidates and directs the finder to emit an advisory finding naming the overlapping ticket id when the plan restates one.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion asserting coverage["overlap"]["status"] == 'ok' on a successful overlap retrieval (the same seeded-store path as AC1).
evidence: 'records a status from the closed set ok, index-absent, catch-up-failed, provider-error'
ACs assert status index-absent, catch-up-failed, provider-error, but none asserts status=='ok'.
AC1 exercises the success path (finding named) but asserts the finding, not the coverage status value.
findings.finding: The closed status set includes 'ok', but no acceptance criterion asserts coverage["overlap"]["status"] == 'ok' on a successful retrieval. Every non-ok member (index-absent, catch-up-failed, provider-error) has a dedicated status-asserting AC; the success member does not.
findings.location: Approach — 'Diagnostic contract' closed set {ok, index-absent, catch-up-failed, provider-error}; Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: A regression that records a wrong/empty status on the success path would be caught by the three failure-status ACs' counterparts but not by any 'ok' assertion.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC1, or add a sibling AC: 'With overlap=True and a matching candidate present, coverage["overlap"]["status"] is ok. Checked by: a test asserting that value.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the overlap-threading inventory from the symbol graph: run_pass1's only src/ caller is ProductionBatchRunner.run at production_batch_runner.py:152 (not review_plan); name the full chain review_plan -> _run_plan_review -> v3 workflow request assembly -> BatchRunRequest.with_inputs -> ProductionBatchRunner.run -> run_pass1, and specify where the overlap flag is injected and read.
evidence: Plan: 'The switch is one keyword-only parameter `overlap: bool = False` on `review_plan` (...:199), threaded to `run_pass1` (`pass1.py:232`) then `_chunk_extra_context`.'

review_plan (__init__.py:199) calls _run_plan_review (__init__.py:265), never run_pass1 directly; _run_plan_review runs the v3 engine workflow (gates/plan-review.yaml), per its docstring at __init__.py:239.

run_pass1's sole src/ call site is production_batch_runner.py:152: `findings = run_pass1(ctx, cfg, runner, single, agent, coverage, req.usd_budget, self._tf_provider)` inside ProductionBatchRunner.run — arguments derived from BatchRunRequest `req`, which carries ad-hoc inputs via req.with_inputs (production_batch_runner.py:123,157,168,175), not an overlap flag.
search_files for run_pass1 across src/ returns exactly one call site (production_batch_runner.py:152); all other src/ hits are docstring/comment references.
findings.finding: The overlap-switch threading inventory for run_pass1 is incomplete: the plan asserts review_plan threads the parameter 'to run_pass1 (pass1.py:232)', but review_plan does not call run_pass1. run_pass1's only src/ caller is ProductionBatchRunner.run at production_batch_runner.py:152, which builds run_pass1's arguments from a BatchRunRequest (req), not from a parameter passed down from review_plan. The intermediate patch sites required to actually carry a boolean from review_plan to run_pass1 are unnamed.
findings.location: Approach, 'On demand, not on every review.': 'The switch is one keyword-only parameter overlap: bool = False on review_plan ... threaded to run_pass1 (pass1.py:232) then _chunk_extra_context.'
scenarios: production_batch_runner.py:152 — the one place that actually invokes run_pass1 — is not in the plan's patch inventory; without threading overlap into BatchRunRequest/req.with_inputs and reading it here, run_pass1 never receives overlap=True and the feature silently never activates on the real review_plan path.

_run_plan_review (__init__.py:339) and the workflow-request assembly between it and ProductionBatchRunner are unnamed intermediate patch sites; a parameter added only to review_plan and run_pass1 has no wire connecting the two, so review_plan(overlap=True) is a no-op.

BatchRunRequest / req.with_inputs is the real carrier for per-run inputs (cf. probe_criteria at production_batch_runner.py:123) and must gain the overlap signal; the plan names none of it, risking an under-delivered Scope where the switch exists but is never read.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry overlap as a BatchRunRequest input (like probe_criteria/relation_snapshot via req.with_inputs): set it where _run_plan_review assembles the workflow/batch request, then read it in ProductionBatchRunner.run and pass it to run_pass1 at production_batch_runner.py:152, which threads it to _chunk_extra_context.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC #2/#3's above-10 candidate limit with ADR 0122's k=5 decision: either justify why the overlap use case can operate at k>10 without the ADR's required `--paired` re-measurement, or add that re-measurement (and an ADR amendment) as plan work.
evidence: AC #2: 'Retrieval offers more than 10 candidates on a store seeded with more than 10 matches. RESULT_LIMIT is 5 ... so retrieval must raise `limit` above its default'
AC #3 injects 'at most 10' candidates, so retrieval is operated at k>10

ADR 0122 decision: 'k=5 is part of the decision, not an implementation detail ... A future change to the surfaced count invalidates this ADR and must re-run --paired' (docs/adr/0122-similar-ticket-retrieval.md:123-126)
ADR 0122 alternatives-rejected: fts5-alone (build nothing) 'is the correct choice if the feature is ever changed to surface 10 results' (:321-323)

lexical.py:14-18 docstring: at k=10 the embedding advantage is 'statistically indistinguishable (p=0.3438), which is the regime where the evidence favours building nothing ... Returning a different count would invalidate the comparison the ADR rests on.'

ABSENCE: the plan's Approach ('Reuse the index; add no second retrieval path') cites ADR 0122's portability but never mentions its k=5 operating-point constraint or any obligation to re-measure when operating at k>10
findings.finding: The plan raises the similar-ticket candidate limit above 10 (AC #2) without considering ADR 0122's load-bearing k=5 decision, which the ADR says any change to the surfaced count invalidates and requires re-running the --paired evaluation.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC line 'Retrieval offers more than 10 candidates ... RESULT_LIMIT is 5'; cross-ref docs/adr/0122-similar-ticket-retrieval.md:123-126,311-323
scenarios: A reviewer or auditor cross-checks the new above-10 retrieval against ADR 0122 and finds the count-change contract (re-run --paired) unmet
Overlap judging at k>10 surfaces candidates in the regime the ADR measured as favouring 'build nothing', where fts5 beats vector on lexical recall@10 (p=0.0000)
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Approach paragraph addressing ADR 0122's operating-point constraint: state why plan-review overlap (full-plan material, advisory, no verdict impact) differs from the create-time k=5 use case such that a larger candidate set is acceptable, OR scope the work to re-run evals/similar-tickets/measure.py --paired at the new k and amend ADR 0122 accordingly. Adjust AC #2/#3 to match whichever path is chosen.
